findings.summary: The owner-gated regressions can wait forever and leak the runtime transaction before their cleanup boundary begins.
findings.diagnosis: Both owner-gated tests create a real initialization owner and then await acquired.wait() before entering the try/finally that opens the gates and reaps the owner. The wait has no timeout, and the repository has no pytest timeout configuration. If initialization stops reaching the patched transaction hook, or cancellation lands during this wait, the test hangs or exits without reaping the owner and can leave _transaction_owner live for later tests.
findings.evidence: The new test executes owner = asyncio.create_task(ensure_initialized_async()) followed by unbounded await acquired.wait() at lines 283-284, while its cleanup starts only at line 285. The touched public-facade test repeats the same ordering at lines 322-323, with its cleanup starting at line 338.
findings.correction: Enter the cleanup try/finally immediately after creating the owner and bound gate acquisition with await asyncio.wait_for(acquired.wait(), timeout=...). In the finally, open both control gates and terminally reap the owner so timeout and cancellation cannot leave transaction ownership behind.
